items.title: Ducks reclaiming mighty status behind youthful scoring surge
items.summary: The way things are going, Anaheim might need to re-insert another word before “Ducks.” Ryan Dixon digs into the Ducks’ scoring surge, among other topics from the week that was in the NHL.
items.body: The way things are going, Anaheim might need to re-insert another word before “Ducks.” Offensive? Might not roll off the tongue, but it’s certainly apt. On Sunday night , the *insert preferred word here* Ducks pumped the Pittsburgh Penguins 5-2 at Honda Center in Orange County. According to the league, Anaheim — winners of five straight — became the eighth team in NHL history to record five or more goals in eight consecutive contests. Cutter Gauthier scored his third goal of the night into an empty net to seal the victory over Pittsburgh. The hat trick was Gauthier's third (!) three-goal game in his past five outings and — after failing to find the net in 10 of his first 11 contests — the Anaheim winger has 13 goals during a six-game goal streak. Gauthier was one of three Ducks to sign significant contracts this summer and, as noted, he’s become a Rocket Richard candidate with 15 goals on the season, one behind the 16 of co-leaders Kirill Kaprizov and Leon Draisaitl. Leo Carlsson , of course, rocked the hockey world with his decision to ink an offer sheet with the Philadelphia Flyers in July. Anaheim matched the deal and the 21-year-old Carlsson — even after being held off the scoresheet versus the Pens — still leads the team with 26 points this year. The contract Anaheim signed that felt like a response to the Carlsson situation was the six-year pact inked by defenceman Tristan Luneau in early September. Carlsson, of course, was never extended before his old deal expired; he became an RFA and the Flyers swooped in with the $18-million cap hit the Ducks then had to match to keep him. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Steven Ellis OAKVILLE, Ont. – And that’s that. The Under-17 World Hockey Challenge in Oakville was one of the first major international tournaments of the year. It showcased the best 15- and 16-year-olds across the world, including a handful of projected early picks for 2028 and 2029. As expected, top 2028 NHL Draft prospect Maddox Schultz was the best player. But it wasn’t enough to get Canada White the championship they were chasing. Instead, the United States pulled through with a 3-0 shutout win over Czechia, while Canada Red beat their national counterparts in the bronze medal game. The tournament had its fair share of blowouts, but that’s to be expected with players this young. The bigger focus was actually how much high-end skill was on display. While Schultz received the most hype, Madden Daneault is the one many expect to go first overall in 2029. And that doesn’t include a host of other quality prospects from those two draft years who took center stage. Today, we’re looking at 10 of the best players from the U-17s in Oakville. We tried to get a fair balance to include every team, but the two squads that finished at the bottom, Finland and Sweden, obviously got a little less love. Each Monday, NHL.com will take a look at what McKenna has done and what's ahead for him with the Gavin McKenna Watch. McKenna had two shots on goal in 15:53 of ice time in a 3-2 loss to the Utah Mammoth on Tuesday, when the Maple Leafs opened a season-long six-game homestand. It was a mixed bag for McKenna against the Montreal Canadiens in a 4-2 loss Saturday. With the puck in the offensive zone, he tried making a rink-wide pass near the blue line that Canadiens forward Chris Kreider intercepted, skated in alone and scored to give Montreal a 3-0 lead at 12:57 of the second period. McKenna sat the remainder of the period but came out strong in the third. After William Nylander scored at 6:19, McKenna made it a one-goal game 55 seconds later. He was first on the puck after an offensive-zone face-off win, rotated into the center of the zone and set up Dakota Joshua for a shot from in front. Goalie Jacob Fowler made the save, but McKenna popped in the rebound at 7:14 to make it 3-2. One night later, McKenna was on the ice for three goals-against in 17:22 of ice time in a 4-0 loss to the New Jersey Devils, their fifth in six games (1-5-0). That was his second-highest ice time this season (17:56 in a 4-1 loss to the New York Islanders on Oct. 17) but also the first game he didn't have a shot on goal. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources What We Learned in Week 6 of Fantasy Hockey Anaheim Ducks players are leading the charge, Brady Tkachuk is a penalty (and stat-covering) machine, and the Chicago Blackhawks are giving Spencer Knight owners headaches. We are now 41 days into the fantasy season and are witnessing teams start to separate in our league standings. It’s a long season, but we are nearing the quarter-mark. Here’s what we learned in Week 6 of fantasy hockey as we try not to overreact while we question what is happening with our goaltenders right now. Gauthier scored in every game during Week 6, extending his historic goal streak to six games with his 13th goal and 44th shot during that stretch. It is the most goals ever during a six-game span, leaving fantasy owners to wonder if they have a potential 70-goal scorer on their hands. The 22-year-old has really turned it on after a slow start to the 2026-27 campaign, where he potted just two goals in his first 11 games. He is now on pace for a whopping 70 goals and 336 SOG across the full 84-game season after missing one game earlier this year. He also led all skaters with three game-winning goals last week, single-handedly dominating that category. Across the last seven days, a surprising seven teams went undefeated as New Jersey (4), Anaheim (4), Nashville (3), Boston (3), New York Rangers (3), Winnipeg (3) and Ottawa (2) all went without a loss. On the other side of the coin, four teams failed to pick up a win as Chicago (4), San Jose (4), Vancouver (3) and Toronto (3) went without a win in Week 6. With both Michael Misa and Gabriel Perreault joining both their teams’ top power-play unit and top line this past week, we are watching more teams lacking offence turn to their young upcoming superstars for immediate solutions.

Now in the final year of a six-year deal, making $36MM by the end of this season, Binnington has begun to fall out of the starting workload he used to boast in St. Louis. The 33-year-old has played just five games in 2026-27, clearly a backup to Joel Hofer , with a singular win to go along with a .851 save percentage and 4.27 goals against average. Hofer, while only having six wins through 12 starts, has a .919 save percentage and 2.36 goals against average. It’s been a downhill trend for Binnington in his time since triumphing in the 2019 Stanley Cup Final victory that earned him a lengthy stay in the Midwest. Since signing his extension, he fell below water to a -36.0 GSAx and a win% of just 46%. Entering their contest yesterday, the Bruins and Panthers ranked in the top five of PIMs in the NHL. They added a combined total of 126 penalties (Florida with 72, Boston with 54) in minutes in their matinee game on Nov. 8 at TD Garden. What was a bruising game from both sides that saw a great many stops in play to assess scrums and infractions, Boston tied its highest single-game total in team PIM’s from 2025-26, which came in a December 21, 2025, 6-2 loss to the Ottawa Senators. items.summary: There are three games on the NHL schedule for Monday. Here are five things to watch, along with the complete game schedule.
items.body: Edmonton captain aims to become fastest to 40 assists; Celebrini, Sharks hope to end skid There are three games on the NHL schedule for Monday. Here are five things to watch, along with the complete game schedule. Connor McDavid looks to extend his season opening 18-game point streak for the Edmonton Oilers (12-3-3) against the New York Rangers at Rogers Place (8 p.m. ET; TVAS, SN+, MSG). The Oilers captain leads the NHL with 47 points (10 goals, 37 assists) and can become the third player in League history to reach 50 points in 19 or fewer games; he has the chance to join Mario Lemieux (1988-89, 1992-93, 1995-96) and Wayne Gretzky (1983-84 , 1984-85). McDavid can also become the fastest player in NHL history to reach 40 assists; Gretzky did so in 22 games in 1984-85. Macklin Celebrini , the No. 1 pick by the San Jose Sharks in the 2024 NHL Draft, can get his 200th career point when they host the New York Islanders at SAP Center (10 p.m. ET; MSGSN, NBCSCA, TVAS). The Sharks captain has 199 points (77 goals, 122 assists) in 169 games and at 20 years, 149 days) can become the fifth-youngest player in League history at the time of his 200th career point, behind Sidney Crosby (19 years, 207 days), Gretzky (19 years, 347 days), Jimmy Carson (20 years, 107 days) and Lemieux (20 years, 133 days on Feb. 15, 1986). Celebrini leads San Jose (7-11-1) this season with 21 points (seven goals, 14 assists) in 17 games and has a three-game point streak (five points; two goals, three assists). For Hellebuyck, the echoes of boos were supposed to be a small taste of things to come for his highly-anticipated return to Winnipeg on Tuesday. items.title: Canadiens’ Arber Xhekaj finding comfort zone in depth role
items.summary: Arber Xhekaj has been providing more evidence of just how comfortable he’s become in the role he had so much trouble nailing down last season. Eric Engels has the story.
items.body: BROSSARD, Que. — There was a sequence in last Tuesday’s game against the Winnipeg Jets that was perfectly indicative of Arber Xhekaj ’s improvement this season, and it came long before he threw his last right-hand cross at Tyrel Bauer’s head. It was in the ninth minute of the second period when Xhekaj set up a great one-timer opportunity in the offensive zone for Adam Engstrom and then hustled back into position in his own end to simultaneously deny a zone entry and a hit from Viggo Bjorck. In both instances, Xhekaj steadied himself, chose the play he was going to make before the puck arrived, and executed to perfection. The pass to Engstrom was the best of several decisions Xhekaj could’ve made in that situation, and it led to a quality scoring chance. And everything he did immediately after that led to the Canadiens continuing one of their only good sequences of the game — and led Bjorck back to the Jets’ bench worse for wear after bearing the brunt of a collision he initiated. That had to feel good for Xhekaj, who was one of roughly five Canadiens who didn’t need a hard look in the mirror after that history-making loss. He was as effective in that game as he had been in each of the 13 games he’d appeared in before it this season, and he’s been just as good since, providing more evidence of just how comfortable he’s become in the role he had so much trouble nailing down last season. items.title: Ducks’ Cutter Gauthier becomes first NHLer with three hat-tricks in a 10-day span to start a month
items.summary: The Swedish-born American set unique history and ranks third in the NHL with 15 goals through 17 games.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Anaheim Ducks forward Cutter Gauthier is enjoying himself this season and making history as the Ducks establish themselves as one of the NHL’s most thrilling teams through the first quarter of the 2026-27 regular season. On Sunday night, with a three-goal, one-assist performance in a 5-2 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins , he became the first player in NHL history to score three hat tricks within the first 10 days of a calendar month. Gauthier leaned on an empty-net goal in the final minute to earn himself the historic honor, as the Ducks became the first team since the 1988-90 LA Kings to score at least five goals in eight consecutive games. The 22-year-old started the month in peak form, scoring his first November hat trick on Nov. 1 in a 6-3 win over the Ottawa Senators . Two days later, he potted another trio against the struggling Vancouver Canucks in a 5-4 victory. Both of his first two hat-tricks in November included two power-play goals, as he makes the most of Anaheim’s league-leading 38.5 percent success rate on the man advantage this season. Yet, his history-making performance against the Penguins didn’t need any special-teams help, with two goals coming at five-on-five before he netted the empty-net marker to seal the victory. Through 17 games this season, the Swedish-born American has 15 goals, good for third in the NHL, and seven assists for 22 points, ranking him 17th in NHL scoring overall. In his career, he has 76 goals and 60 assists for 136 points in 176 games with the Ducks and, previously, the Philadelphia Flyers . After Sunday’s win, the Ducks sit third in the Pacific Division with 21 points through the first 18 games of the 84-game campaign, as they look ahead to a Wednesday night home game against the Nashville Predators.

Devils general manager Sunny Mehta announced Hellebuyck will not play against his former team, the Winnipeg Jets, at Canada Life Centre. The team is expected to start Jake Allen instead. Mehta made the announcement in a statement released by the team following Hellebuyck making 23 saves in a 4-0 win against the Toronto Maple Leafs at Scotiabank Arena on Sunday, his first shutout since New Jersey acquired him from the Jets on Oct. 23. New Jersey coach Sheldon Keefe said the decision relates to the Devils keeping a close eye on Hellebuyck's workload as he gets into the flow of the season after not participating in training camp or preseason games. "This has been an organizational decision for us that we've debated at length," Mehta said. "Connor Hellebuyck was adamant that he felt a duty to play on Tuesday in Winnipeg. However, in our estimation, playing in this game would potentially give us a reduction in our expected win probability. Even though Connor isn't playing, at his request, we will coordinate a media availability after Tuesday's morning skate at Canada Life Centre." Hellebuyck, who spoke to the media following the game Sunday, reiterated Mehta's statement about him being adamant about playing in Winnipeg. Renowned as the father, even godfather, of Russian hockey, Anatoly Tarasov has had an influence on the game in his native country and far beyond that remains strong more than three decades after his 1995 death. Today, Alexey is working to promote and protect the legacy of one of hockey’s great builders as he presides over the developmental Golden Puck youth tournament that his grandfather founded in 1964. "It's one of those things you always talk about the guys you want to thank and there's never enough time to go through all the names, but these are definitely three of the guys that helped me get there, and now it's their opportunity to get what they deserve," Weber told NHL.com. Weber and Rinne played together in the American Hockey League with Milwaukee in 2005-06, and for eight seasons in the NHL with the Nashville Predators (2008-16). He became teammates with Price in Montreal when the Predators traded him to the Canadiens for P.K. Subban on June 29, 2016. They played together for five seasons. items.body: 19-year-old applies lessons learned from dad to bring back defunct program William Douglas has been writing The Color of Hockey blog since 2012. Douglas joined NHL.com in 2019 and writes about people of color in the sport. Today, he profiles Danna Ramadan, a goalie with Egypt’s women’s hockey team. She successfully led the effort to revive the women’s club hockey team at Rutgers University in New Jersey this season. Danna Ramadan couldn’t imagine going to a college without being able to play hockey. “I’ve been around hockey my entire life,” said Ramadan, a 19-year-old goalie from Somerset, New Jersey. “There really was no world where I wouldn't be playing hockey in college. It was just about which route I would take.” Ramadan created her own route by reviving Rutgers University women’s club hockey team, which had been defunct since 2019. items.body: WINNIPEG — Brayden Yager was grinning ear to ear while surrounded by reporters following a roller-coaster Sunday night at Canada Life Centre. The 21-year-old Winnipeg forward had just notched his first NHL goal — which was also his first NHL point — to help lift the Jets to an eventful 4-3 victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning. What made the milestone extra special was the small family cheering section sitting rinkside that shared in the meaningful moment. “Mom, dad and grandpa were here, so it was pretty cool to do it in front of them," Yager said after the game, still dripping with sweat. "Unbelievable feeling. Dream come true.” The Saskatchewan native's memorable moment was born out of a bloody sequence early in the third period. Winnipeg (7-8-3) was already protecting a 2-0 lead on second-period goals from Cole Perfetti and Morgan Barron when Lightning forward Pontus Holmberg caught Yager in the mouth with a high stick. The infraction drew blood, resulting in a four-minute double-minor penalty and a quick check-in with the team's medical staff. Yager was back on the ice moments later. With nine seconds remaining in the first minor, he fired a one-timer past Tampa Bay goaltender Andrei Vasilevskiy after a slick deflected feed from fellow rookie Viggo Bjorck. "Just a great play by Viggo there that touched over to me and I had a pretty wide-open net," Yager said. "You can definitely feel it, the atmosphere. I thought the fans were unbelievable tonight." Now, he’s off the roster altogether, as the team announced ( Twitter link ) that they’ve returned Chromiak to AHL Ontario. The 24-year-old was brought up about a week and a half ago but didn’t see much action, getting into just two games. That said, they were Chromiak’s first two appearances at the NHL level. With the Kings operating very tight to the cap ceiling this season, Chromiak’s assignment now gives them enough cap space to be able to bring someone up should more injuries arise. items.body: Register Login Panthers Recall Jack Devine By Brian La Rose | at November 8, 2026 6:46 pm Prior to their game against Boston this afternoon, the Panthers added some extra depth to their forward group. The team announced that they’ve recalled winger Jack Devine from AHL Charlotte. The 23-year-old was a seventh-round pick back in 2021, going 221st overall in 2022 and has clearly outperformed that draft selection. After a strong four seasons at the University of Denver (including tallying 56 and 57 points in his final two years), Devine turned pro last season, playing predominantly with the Checkers. Devine’s recall comes on the heels of the injury that Sandis Vilmanis sustained on Saturday. The 34-year-old underwent hip surgery over the summer, and back in September it was thought he’d be out until December, returning considerably sooner than expected. Going from an ECHLer to a two-time Stanley Cup champion and legitimate top-six threat, Gourde returned to Tampa after 3 1/2 years with the Kraken. A beloved veteran no longer expected to drive the same amount of offense, he suited up for all 82 games last year recording 28 points. It was the fourth time the spark plug surpassed the 100-hit mark, landing 115. Facing multiple first round playoff exits, the Lightning made an effort to strengthen their middle-six along with adding a star in John Carlson . The Blackhawks, in a rebuild for the better part of a decade, were intending this to be a season in which they turned a corner. Instead, they've started the year 4-13-1 — better only than the lowly Vancouver Canucks in the Western Conference. Things hit a low point with a 9-2 loss to the Carolina Hurricanes on Saturday night. The Blackhawks were off Sunday and don't play again until Thursday, which led many to wonder whether regime change is imminent. Instead, it appears general manager Kyle Davidson is giving Blashill some more time to right the ship. The former Detroit Red Wings coach was hired by Chicago ahead of the 2025-26 season. However, Del Gaizo has made a strong impression in the Rangers organization and offers 55 games of NHL experience, fully capable of entering the lineup. A native of Basking Ridge, New Jersey, the 27-year-old was picked in the fourth round of the 2019 draft by Nashville out of UMass-Amherst. He was a high-impact freshman with 29 points in 41 games, teammate of Cale Makar , former Ranger Zachary Jones , as well as another NHLer Matthew Kessel . Boasting an elite blue line, the Minutemen made it to the National Championship game. Turning professional two years later, Del Gaizo peaked with 46 games for the Preds in 2024-25, recording nine points, and having yet to skate in an NHL game since then. Spending last season with the Laval Rocket (Canadiens), Del Gaizo caught on with his childhood favorite team on a two-year contract. items.title: Two NHL players placed on waivers for Nov. 8
items.summary: Arvid Soderblom looks to be getting sent back to the AHL after a tough start to the season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images A couple of netminders have hit the wire. On Sunday, the Chicago Blackhawks placed goaltender Arvid Soderblom on waivers, with the Washington Capitals doing the same with fellow backstop Remi Poirier. Soderblom entered the 2026-27 season set to be the backup to Spencer Knight once again. However, while the Blackhawks have struggled as a whole, Soderblom’s play has been anything but up to par. In five appearances so far, four starts, the 27-year-old has allowed 21 goals, giving him a 4.67 goals-against average and a .842 save percentage, along with a 0-3-1 record. Who the Hawks would call up to take his place is yet to be determined. Drew Commesso has been with the organization the longest, having played a couple of games with Chicago on top of his time with the AHL’s Rockford IceHogs, but Stanislav Berezhnoy has had better numbers early on this year with Rockford. In 117 NHL games, Soderblom has a record of 25-68-15, with a 3.65 GAA, a .885 SV% and one shutout. He’s in the final season of his two-year contract extension, which he signed in July 2025. The deal carries an AAV of $2.75 million. Poirier was acquired by the Capitals last Sunday in exchange for a seventh-round pick from the New Jersey Devils , as the Devils had to make some roster moves after receiving Connor Hellebuyck from the Winnipeg Jets . Poirier, who was claimed off waivers by the Devils from the Dallas Stars , has yet to play a game this season. He has spent the past three seasons with the Stars’ top farm team, the Texas Stars. In 137 regular-season games in the AHL, the 25-year-old is 70-51-16, with a 2.76 GAA, a .908 SV% and six shutouts. He’s also 11-9 in 23 Calder Cup Playoff contests, with a 2.42 GAA, a .909 SV% and three shutouts.

The former University of Michigan star made it clear he wasn’t interested in planting roots with the club who had drafted him 14th overall in 2022. He was traded in August 2024 to the Penguins in exchange for Brayden Yager , becoming the club’s top forward prospect and looking to be an instant contributor who could play alongside Sidney Crosby . items.summary: TORONTO -- Carey Price shares one thing in common with every goaltender who played in his era -- the former Montreal Canadiens goalie never liked facing Alex Ovechkin and his one-timer from the left face-off circle.
items.body: Price reflects on facing Ovechkin's one-timer; Bergeron, Rinne, Curley cite favorite teams; Tkachuk says father 'true Bostonian' TORONTO -- Carey Price shares one thing in common with every goaltender who played in his era -- the former Montreal Canadiens goalie never liked facing Alex Ovechkin and his one-timer from the left face-off circle. "I think everyone knows the answer to this question," Price said, smiling as he talked. "He gets over there in a spot and he gets to wire one a hundred miles at you from 30 feet away 12 times a game." Price offered that obvious tidbit about Ovechkin, the NHL's all-time leader with 930 goals, at the ESSO Inductee Fan Forum inside the Great Hall at the Hockey Hall of Fame on Sunday. The Fan Forum, an annual event at Hockey Hall of Fame Weekend, is an hour-long intimate Q&A session where fans in attendance are given the opportunity to ask the player inductees questions that typically range from career highlights and memories to advice they would offer to kids who want to be like them. The Class of 2026 Hockey Hall of Fame inductees share their thoughts Price, sitting on the dais with fellow Class of 2026 inductees Keith Tkachuk and Pekka Rinne to his right, and Cindy Curley and Patrice Bergeron to his left, talked about Ovechkin in response to a question from a bilingual Canadiens fan who said he was from Sturgeon Falls, Ontario. "He always seemed to bring his best, especially when he came to Montreal," Price said. "He's just a competitive guy by nature and he just brought it when he played specifically, I think. He eventually caught on with Seattle as an undrafted free agent. Jeremy Swayman made 40 saves, 17 coming in the first period, for the Bruins, who improved to 7-0-0 at home by winning their fourth straight game a day after placing young star James Hagens on injured reserve. JJ Peterka added a goal for Boston, which owns a plus-21 goal differential at TD Garden. David Pastrnak and Pavel Zacha each added two assists. Carter Verhaeghe scored a power-play goal for the Panthers, and Jacob Markstrom stopped 32 shots. Florida has lost three of four games. Boston’s six-foot-seven defenceman Nikita Zadorov dropped the gloves against six-foot-one forward Brady Tkachuk at the opening faceoff, setting the stage for 126 total penalty minutes. Just over six minutes later, Florida’s Garnet Hathaway squared off against forward Mark Kastelic. The Panthers swept the three games against Boston last season, winning each by one goal. Following a lengthy review, Lindholm was credited with a goal that made it 1-0 just 4:50 into the game after his wrister broke off Markstrom and trickled behind him, nearing the goal line as he attempted to pull it back with his glove. Eyssimont poked a loose puck into the net following his wraparound shot, making it 2-0 less than two minutes later. Geekie then scored for the fourth straight game, one-timing a shot for a power-play goal at 15:59 with the Bruins on a two-man advantage. The Bruins, who entered with the NHL’s second-best goal differential behind Carolina, were off since rolling to a 6-2 victory at Pittsburgh on Thursday. items.summary: The Edmonton Oilers have placed defenseman Atro Leppanen on waivers for the purpose of AHL assignment.
items.body: Register Login Oilers’ Atro Leppanen Clears Waivers By Brian La Rose | at November 8, 2026 2:30 pm November 8: Leppanen made it through the wire unclaimed, Elliotte Friedman of Sportsnet shared today . He’ll look to build off a nice start to his North American career last season in Bakersfield and vie for a call-up sometime ahead. November 7: After missing the first six weeks of the season, Oilers defenseman Atro Leppanen appears to be ready to return. The team announced today that they’ve placed the blueliner on waivers for the purpose of assignment to AHL Bakersfield. It would be fair to call the 27-year-old a late bloomer. As recently as the 2022-23 season, he had been playing back home in Finland in the second-tier Mestis league and wasn’t even remotely on the NHL radar. But a strong showing that season that saw him record 58 points in just 51 games gave Leppanen a shot to move up to the Liiga level with Sport. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Wendell Cruz The NHL’s Department of Player Safety announced Sunday that New York Islanders defenseman Logan Stanley has been fined $3,865 for slashing New Jersey Devils forward Nico Hischier. items.body: Logan Stanley is facing some discipline after a net-front tussle. The New York Islanders defenceman has been fined $3,865.98, the maximum amount allowable under the collective bargaining agreement, for slashing New Jersey Devils forward Nico Hischier , the NHL's department of player safety announced Sunday. The incident occurred in the second period of Saturday's 5-4 Devils overtime win. Near the end of the frame, Stanley laid into the net-front Hischier, forcing the Devils captain onto the ice. As Hischier got up, he poked at Stanley, to which the Islanders defenceman retaliated with a hard slash, sending Hischier to the ice once more, then pushed him while he was already down. The two players then exchanged some words and a scrum ensued after play was called dead. Stanley received two minor penalties on the play — one for the slash and another for roughing as part of the scrum. The 28-year-old Kitchener, Ont., native leads the Islanders in penalty minutes with 34 in his first year with the team. He also had five assists in 16 games.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Bruce Kluckhohn-Imagn Images When you think of the Minnesota Wild’s top offensive weapons, you think of Kirill Kaprizov or Quinn Hughes, right? Through the first month of the season, Eriksson Ek, a player that many love as a solid two-way center, has been one of the surprising scoring threats for the Wild. Through 17 games, the 29-year-old has posted six goals and nine assists for 15 points, placing him tied for third in goals and assists, and fourth in overall scoring. If he manages to stay healthy and keep scoring at that rate, he’ll blow his previous career best, 64 points in 2023-24, out of the water. On Friday’s edition of Daily Faceoff LIVE , Brock Seguin joined Tyler Yaremchuk to discuss how impressive Eriksson Ek has been in the early going this year. Brock Seguin: For me, just because he was a player that I was really high on coming into the season …He’s been great thus far. 15 points in 17 games. Six of those are assists. He’s on pace for 74 points, 30 goals. The 74 points would blow away his previous career high. Really nice start for him. items.summary: The Washington Capitals’ Tom Wilson won’t face further discipline after his actions on Saturday night.
items.body: The Washington Capitals ' Tom Wilson won't face further discipline after his actions on Saturday. Wilson delivered a hard hit to the back of Florida Panthers ' Sandis Vilmanis in the first period that sent the forward headfirst into the area where the glass meets the boards. Vilmanis left the game and did not return, and Wilson received a major penalty for boarding and a game misconduct for the play. After speculation about whether Wilson would face a hearing for the hit, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported Sunday that he's hearing the Capitals' star will not face supplemental discipline. Panthers coach Paul Maurice said after the game that Florida was waiting on more information about Vilmanis' condition. “Getting looked at by another doctor tomorrow," he said. "But probably we’ll have to wait until we get him back to see our guys before we have a real good idea, get some imaging.” Wilson has been suspended several times during his 14-year career. He was given 20 games for a blindside hit to the head in 2018, a ban later reduced to 14 games on appeal after he had already served 16. He received a seven-game suspension for boarding Boston’s Brandon Carlo with head contact in 2021 and six games in 2024 for a stick to the face of Toronto Maple Leafs forward Noah Gregor. The 22-year-old Vilmanis had his first career two-goal game Wednesday night when Florida beat Chicago.

items.body: Geoff Burke-USA TODAY Sports Geoff Burke-USA TODAY Sports USA Hockey Domination Continues At U17 World Challenge, Maddox Schultz Shines Ken Campbell Partner Nov 8, 2026 2:45 PM Published Nov 8, 2026 2:45 PM After Team USA captured gold at the under-17 World Challenge hockey tournament on Saturday, Ken Campbell breaks down some of the standout prospects to keep an eye on for the 2028 NHL draft. Anyone hoping or expecting USA's run of international hockey success to come to an end anytime soon would undoubtedly be disappointed Saturday night after Team USA won the under-17 World Challenge hockey tournament with a 3-0 win over Czechia in the final. The Americans, the only team of the six in the tournament that plays together all season, was full marks for its win. Canada, which split its 44 players into Canada Red and Canada White, were a disappointment. Red beat White 8-4 in a bronze medal game that featured very little intensity or physicality and even less good goaltending. More Videos But Maddox Schultz, the early favorite to go No. 1 in the 2028 NHL draft, did not disappoint, leading the tournament in goals (six), assists (10) and points (16). items.title: Norway says team will be replaced by Russia for 2027 World Juniors
items.summary: Norway is the lowest-ranked team heading into this year’s tournament, meaning they’re the first to be eliminated with Russia’s return.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Steven Ellis/Daily Faceoff The first casualty of a recent court ruling has become official. In a release on Sunday, the Norwegian Ice Hockey Association announced that its national junior team has been officially removed from the 2027 IIHF World Junior Championship. Russia will be taking their place at the upcoming event in Edmonton and Red Deer, Alta. Petter Salsten, the NIHA’s Secretary General, stated the the federation is still waiting for more information from the IIHF. “We are aware of the status and the measures the IIHF feels compelled to take, and will await further information from the IIHF in the coming days,” Salsten said in a translated statement . “We have previously made it clear where we stand on the issue of Russia’s participation, where we believe they should not be able to participate internationally as long as the war in Ukraine continues. This also clearly shows all the practical challenges and immediate consequences for everyone involved when countries are to be reinstated immediately.” Earlier this month, the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled that Russia must be allowed to participate in IIHF tournaments, ending the latter organization’s over four-year-ban. The CAS cited that the IIHF didn’t provide enough evidence to keep Russia from competing. The IIHF has stated its displeasure with the decision, with many nations, including Finland, Sweden and Norway, stating that they will refuse to play Russia in international games. Canadian prime minister Mark Carney stated that Russia will not be allowed to come to the World Juniors next month, something that Salsten hopes could lead to a change in Norwegian team’s fate. items.title: Canadiens’ Jacob Fowler had apple thrown at him during game against Leafs
items.summary: Fowler was hit with some produce during the second period of Saturday night’s matchup in Toronto.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: John E. Sokolowski-Imagn Images What have you seen thrown on the ice during a hockey game? Hats, cephalopods, rubber rats, chickens, tennis balls and bras have landed on the playing surface over the NHL’s illustrious history. That’s apparently what went flying at Scotiabank Arena on Saturday night during a game between the Toronto Maple Leafs and Montreal Canadiens . During the second period, a fan threw a green apple toward Canadiens goaltender Jacob Fowler, seemingly trying to get the young netminder off his game. After the game, which saw Montreal skate away with a 4-2 victory over their historic rivals, Fowler admitted that the apple actually hit him during the play. During a humorous moment after play had stopped, Fowler stated that he and the ref were discussing whether a goal against him would’ve counted. In the moment, Fowler was aggravated, but afterward, he was able to make light of the situation. The act of distraction did little to get Fowler off his game. The 21-year-old made 26 saves, earning his eighth win of the season, placing him tied for fifth in that category among backstops league-wide. While Fowler started the 2026-27 with the Canadiens’ American Hockey League affiliate, the Laval Rocket, the Boston College product has been a mainstay on the Montreal roster since Samuel Montembeault suffered an injury in October. After dropping his first start of the season, Fowler has helped won eight of his last nine starts, only squandering a point during that chaotic game against the Winnipeg Jets last Tuesday. items.title: Will the star player trade requests eventually balance out, or is it a sign of a bigger trend?
items.summary: Nikita Kucherov’s trade demand isn’t all that similar to the exits of Connor Hellebuyck and others.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The era of player demands in the NHL has arrived. With the likes of Brady Tkachuk, Connor Hellebuyck, and Quinn Hughes demanding their way out of their Canadian teams to sign with U.S. NHL clubs, a burgeoning trend of superstars taking the future into their own hands is emerging. So when Tampa Bay Lightning star Nikita Kucherov requested a trade, it came as a shock—and for some, followed a similar trend to other stars around the league. On a recent episode of Daily Faceoff LIVE , co-hosts Tyler Yaremchuk and Carter Hutton broke down whether the recent moves are just the start of a trend, or whether the situation could even out as the salary cap grows. Tyler Yaremchuk: With all these star players requesting trades, was this a coming trend because the salary cap is rising after a flat COVID era, or is it a small window of time with just a few players that will balance out? I think it’s more the latter, and this will balance out at some point. I think you’ll also get kind of a counter-movement of guys who want to be loyal, and I also think the Kucherov thing is totally different. I wanted to highlight a quote from Brandon Hagel yesterday. Hagel said: “He’s done everything he possibly could for the city. It’s not like he committed here for eight years and asked out two years into it.” This is a different situation, and I agree with Hagel, and I think it’s bang on. items.title: Sunday Overreactions: Will Blackhawks’ rebuild ever turn a corner?
items.summary: The Blackhawks have missed the playoffs six years in a row and appear headed for a seventh. Has their rebuild hit a wall? Michael Amato discusses that and more in Sunday Overreactions.
items.body: It’s early November and the Chicago Blackhawks are in a familiar spot. Second-to-last in the NHL, with a league-worst minus-37 goal differential and barreling through another season that feels destined to be lost. The pain of a rebuild is usually a small price to pay for three Stanley Cups from Chicago’s previous core, but this one has been particularly agonizing. The Blackhawks have missed the playoffs six years in a row and appear headed for a seventh. There also doesn’t seem to be many positive signs to build on going forward. Sure, Connor Bedard looks every bit of a superstar in the making, though there aren’t many running mates who are going to help the Blackhawks captain imminently. Rebuilds take time, but it’s important that an organization is moving in the right direction and there’s a light at the end of the tunnel. I’m not sure anyone can say that about Chicago right now. This is Bedard’s fourth season and the team has never finished any higher than 31st since he joined the NHL. Where are the Blackhawks right now in the standings? You guessed it, 31st. Bedard needs more help. Theoretically, that help should be coming, considering all the high draft picks Chicago has had in recent years. The Blackhawks picked in the first round 11 times between 2022-2025, which included a first overall (Bedard), second overall (Artyom Levshunov), third overall (Anton Frondell) and seventh overall (Kevin Korchinski). Frondell, Levshunov and others still have a ton of potential and patience is needed, but there is far less confidence in many of the other first-rounders the Blackhawks bet on. items.title: Canucks match effort by high-powered Oilers but crumble in third period
items.summary: It was a distinctly better effort than the Canucks managed in Thursday’s lifeless loss. But their opponent was much better too.
items.body: EDMONTON — When you are playing hockey until nearly midnight, typically you either have the cheaper ice time in your beer league or are playing in overtime in the Stanley Cup Playoffs. The Vancouver Canucks and Edmonton Oilers were doing neither on Saturday night. It was merely Game 19 for the Canucks, who at least for a while played playoff-like hockey even though they are the National Hockey League team most likely to be the first one eliminated from playoff contention this season. The Canucks competed admirably against the Oilers, a legitimate Stanley Cup contender, but surrendered two goals in three minutes early in the third period and lost the late-night game 4-2. It was a distinctly better effort than the Canucks managed in Thursday’s lifeless 6-2 loss to the Winnipeg Jets. But their opponent was much better, too. “A lot of, really, positives coming out of it, especially the first two periods, in terms of just the overall effort,” Vancouver coach Manny Malhotra said. “The attention to detail was there and because of that, we were in a situation going into third where we had an opportunity to win. “Again, it comes down to just those momentary lapses in detail and small missed assignments or a missed puck battle. Those are the things that add up. items.title: Penguins’ Sidney Crosby moves to sixth all-time in NHL scoring
items.summary: Crosby recorded his 1,772nd career point and passed Marcel Dionne for sixth on the NHL’s all-time list.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Sidney Crosby moved into sole possession of sixth place on the NHL’s all-time points list after he scored twice to help the Pittsburgh Penguins win 5-2 over the Los Angeles Kings Saturday night. Crosby passed Hockey Hall of Famer Marcel Dionne with his 1,772nd point after he deflected the puck past Kings goaltender Darcy Kuemper in the second period. He scored an empty netter to seal the win for Pittsburgh. The 39-year-old now has six goals and six assists for 12 points in 17 games this season. In 2025-26, Crosby passed Mario Lemieux and Steve Yzerman for eighth and seventh all-time in points, respectively. He now needs 26 points to pass Hall of Famer Ron Francis for fifth on the all-time list. Across 21 NHL seasons, Crosby has 660 goals and 1,113 assists for 1,773 points in 1,437 career regular-season games. He has hit the 100-point mark in six seasons and recorded at least 50 assists in a season 12 times. During that time, he’s broken the 100-point mark six times, recorded at least 50 assists 12 times, hit the 30-goal mark 13 times and has averaged more than a point-per-game in every season of his career. Crosby also has 72 goals and 134 assists for 206 points in 186 career playoff games. He captained the Penguins to three Stanley Cup championships in 2009, 2016 and 2017, and helped them reach the Stanley Cup Final in 2008. He also won the Conn Smythe Trophy in both 2016 and 2017. Crosby has twice won each of the Hart Trophy, the Art Ross Trophy, the Maurice “Rocket” Richard Trophy and the Ted Lindsay Award.

items.body: EDMONTON -- Ryan Nugent-Hopkins sustained an apparent head injury 45 seconds into the second period of a 4-2 win for the Edmonton Oilers against the Vancouver Canucks at Rogers Place on Saturday and did not return to the game. The forward was hit on the side of the head with an attempted shoot-in by Oilers defenseman Ryan Shea. Nugent-Hopkins left the ice immediately and did not return. “I don’t think he is (going to miss much time), actually,” Edmonton coach Mike Babcock said after the game. “Initially, you’re worried about a broken jaw and they did an assessment on that. Just knowing our medical guys, there will probably be more assessments tomorrow. But I just shook his hand, he was in the hallway and seemed to be doing OK.” The 33-year-old has 11 points (four goals, seven assists) in nine games. He missed the first nine games of the season with a lower-body injury and made his season debut in a 6-5 shootout win against the Carolina Hurricanes on Oct. 22. Nugent-Hopkins broke the Oilers all-time games played record in a 4-3 shootout loss at the New Jersey Devils on Tuesday, playing in his 1,038th game. Selected by Edmonton with the No. 1 pick in the 2011 NHL Draft, Nugent-Hopkins is in his 16th season and has 815 points (295 goals, 520 assists) in 1,040 games.

items.body: Facebook icon Twitter icon Reddit icon Copy icon Link Copied Add RMNB as a preferred source on Google Two of the NHL’s best young defensemen showed off a different side of their games on Saturday night. Rather than creating offense, Matthew Schaefer and Luke Hughes exchanged punches late in the second period of their heated Metropolitan Division rivalry matchup between the New York Islanders and New Jersey Devils . The two were the main event of a fracas that saw five separate roughing penalties called as tempers flared around New York’s net. The conflict started in front of the Islanders’ net after Logan Stanley slashed Devils forward Nico Hischier and tussled with defenseman Brett Pesce . Attention then turned behind the net, where Schaefer and Hughes turned up the temperature to 11 as they threw gloved haymakers at each other’s faces, and Schaefer ended up on top of Hughes in a pile-up. “I don’t know,” Hughes said . “He just had my visor, and we just started…it doesn’t really matter. I think hockey is an emotional sport, and I wouldn’t call that a fight at all. Neither of us had our gloves off. It’s part of the game, two competitive guys.” Schaefer, who scored his fifth goal of the season in the game, shared a very similar take on the play. “I don’t know,” Schaefer said . “I think it was just kind of roughing up a bit. Just kind of grabbing each other.” The heated disagreement is very out of character for both players, as neither the 19-year-old Schaefer nor the 23-year-old Hughes has ever gotten into an NHL fight. Schaefer maxed out at 38 penalty minutes in his rookie 2025-26 campaign, while Hughes has never recorded more than 32 penalty minutes in a season during his parts of five years with the Devils. items.body: LOS ANGELES — Sidney Crosby scored two goals while moving into sole possession of sixth place on the NHL’s career scoring list, and the Pittsburgh Penguins snapped their four-game skid with a 5-2 victory over the Los Angeles Kings on Saturday night. The 39-year-old Crosby broke his tie with Kings great Marcel Dionne by scoring his 1,772nd point when Evgeni Malkin’s one-timer deflected in off him in the second period. Crosby added a late empty-net goal, diving face-first on the ice to tip it home. Tommy Novak got two goals in the first six minutes and Egor Chinakhov also scored for the Penguins, who moved Crosby and the 40-year-old Malkin onto their top line before the game in an effort to spark their struggling lineup. Corey Perry and Alex Laferriere scored and Darcy Kuemper stopped only 14 shots for the Kings, who have lost two of the last three during their seven-game homestand. Novak put the Pens ahead less than two minutes after the opening faceoff after controlling a rebound in front. Less than 3 1/2 minutes later, he carried the puck into the zone and followed behind Ben Kindel to cash in another rebound for his seventh career multi-goal game. Perry scored midway through the first when Mikey Anderson's high shot off the end boards ricocheted down toward the crease, where he slapped it out of mid-air for the second goal of his 22nd NHL season. Fowler made 36 saves before five Jets shots found the back of his net, and then he had to sit with that awful feeling until the start of Saturday’s game in Toronto. items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that Los Angeles’ Alex Laferriere preceded the puck into the offensive zone and was in an off-side position prior to the goal. According to Rule 38.9, “The standard for overturning the call in the event of a “GOAL” call on the ice is that the NHL Situation Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the On-Ice Official(s), determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an “Off-Side” infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed.” The clock is reset to show 4:29 (15:31 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.

items.title: Oilers’ Connor McDavid ties Adam Oates with assists in 18 consecutive games
items.body: Connor McDavid is taking a real run at one of Wayne Gretzky's records. The Edmonton Oilers star notched an assist in his 18th consecutive game to start the season on Saturday. McDavid set up Mattias Ekholm for the first goal of the night in the first period against the visiting Vancouver Canucks. McDavid moved into a tie with Adam Oates (1992-93, Boston Bruins) for second on the NHL list of most consecutive games with an assist. Another Hall of Famer, Gretzky, owns the record with 23 games in a row with an assist, set in 1990-91 with the Oilers. If McDavid can keep his run going, he'd be able to tie and break the record in Florida and Tampa Bay on Nov. 17 and 19. McDavid entered the night with a league-leading 44 points, 13 ahead of teammate Leon Draisaitl in the NHL scoring race.

items.body: EDMONTON — Leon Draisaitl had two goals and an assist and Connor McDavid added three assists as the Edmonton Oilers came away with a 4-2 victory over the struggling Vancouver Canucks on Saturday. Mattias Ekholm and Jason Dickinson also scored for the Oilers (12-3-3) who snapped a two-game losing skid. The Oilers are 10-0-2 when they score first this season. Devon Levi returned from injury to record 20 saves and improve to 7-1-0 in the Edmonton net. Max Sasson and Brock Boeser replied for the Canucks (3-15-1) who have lost five straight and 15 of their last 16. Canucks: Swedish forward Liam Öhgren was unable to extend his scoring streak to three games. The 22-year-old had scored four goals in his previous five games, including his first-ever power-play goal. Oilers: McDavid extended his season-starting points and assists streak to 18 games. He now leads the league with 10 goals, 37 assists and 47 points. The Oilers captain matched Adam Oates for the second-longest assist streak in NHL history behind only Wayne Gretzky’s 23 games set in 1990-91. McDavid also became the sixth player in NHL history with a season-opening 18-game point streak. Edmonton took a 3-1 lead four minutes into the final frame as their potent power play struck when McDavid sent it across to Draisaitl and he unleashed his patented one-timer for his 15th of the season. Evan Bouchard extended his points streak to six games and both he and Draisaitl have points in 16 of 18 games. items.title: Jack Hughes scores in overtime as Devils rally past Islanders
items.body: NEW YORK — Jack Hughes scored in overtime to lift the New Jersey Devils to a 5-4 victory over the New York Islanders on Saturday. Dougie Hamilton, Luke Evangelista, Declan Chisholm and Evan Rodrigues also scored for New Jersey, which extended its winning streak to four games. Jake Allen made 19 saves. Hughes scored with 3:42 remaining in overtime, keeping the puck on a two-on-one rush before firing a shot past Ilya Sorokin’s blocker. Anthony Duclair, Matthew Schaefer, Simon Holmstrom and Victor Eklund scored for New York, which lost its third straight game. Sorokin finished with 45 saves and captain Bo Horvat added two assists. The Devils erased a two-goal deficit in the third period, capped by Hamilton’s power-play goal with 6:18 remaining in regulation. Jack Hughes curled around the net before finding Hamilton in the slot for the tying goal. Evangelista started the comeback when he pulled New Jersey within a goal at 6:08 of the third period. The Islanders took a 2-1 lead after the first period. Duclair opened the scoring with less than five minutes remaining, Rodrigues tied it 17 seconds later and Schaefer put New York back ahead with his fifth goal of the season. Chisholm tied the score at 2 just 4:42 into the second period when Jesper Bratt fired a shot off the end boards that took an awkward bounce around the net, allowing Chisholm to bury the rebound. Two of Islanders goaltender Ilya Sorokin’s best saves came against Devils captain Nico Hischier. Sorokin denied Hischier on a breakaway in the closing seconds of the second period and stopped a one-timer in the opening minute of the third.

items.body: An apple nearly took a bite out of Montreal Canadiens goaltender Jacob Fowler on Saturday. The apple found its way to the ice during the second period of a game between the Canadiens and Maple Leafs in Toronto. Referee TJ Luxmore was seen on camera holding it up to Fowler before disposing of it. Fowler told Sportsnet's Kyle Bukauskas after the game that the apple wasn't real but added that it was still one of the weirdest things he'd ever seen hit the ice. "I was pretty dialled in but I saw an apple come on the ice right in front of me. I'm used to tracking a black puck not a green apple," Fowler said with a laugh. "I saw that one and (Luxmore) told me he would have blown the play dead if they had gotten in the zone so thankfully they didn't get one there." The flying apple didn't faze Fowler, who stopped 26 saves in a 4-2 win.

Both games will take place at Veikkaus Arena in Helsinki, roughly a seven hour drive south of Kokko’s hometown of Oulu. He played much of his junior and early pro career close to Oulu. Kokko has served as the starter for the AHL’s Coachella Valley Firebirds to start the season. He has set a 4-3-3 record and .893 save percentage through 10 games so far. While a meager stat-line, Kokko has outperformed backup Victor Ostman , who has a 1-2-1 record and .872 save percentage through four games. Kokko has served as Coachella Valley’s starter through the last two seasons, combining for a 39-20-4 record and .907 save percentage through 68 games. He has also made four appearances in the NHL, marked by a 1-2-0 record and .875 save percentage. The Finnish goaltender will only be available if both Joey Daccord and Philipp Grubauer become unavailable during the back-to-back games. If not, he’ll enjoy a trip with Finnish compatriots Kaapo Kakko and Jani Nyman .

items.body: After missing the past nine games with an undisclosed upper-body injury, Byram's agent is attempting to provide a bit of clarity on the situation. "Darren Ferris reached out to me today," Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman said on Saturday Headlines. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Toronto Maple Leafs announced on social media that defenseman Morgan Rielly left Saturday’s game against the Montreal Canadiens with a lower-body injury and would not return. It’s not clear how or when Rielly sustained the injury, but he left the bench during the first period. He finished the night with 5:45 of ice time on eight shifts. Going into Saturday’s game, Rielly had 12 assists and averaged 19:31 of ice time in 17 games in 2026-27. Now in his 14th NHL season, Rielly had 98 goals and 463 assists for 561 points in 968 career regular-season games. Since entering the league in 2013-14, Rielly has recorded three 50-assist seasons and has four seasons where he recorded at least 50 points. His best season came in 2018-19 when he posted 20 goals and 52 assists for 72 points. That season, he finished fifth in Norris Trophy voting and fourth in the Lady Byng Trophy vote. Rielly, a native of Vancouver, also has 15 goals and 32 assists for 47 points in 70 Stanley Cup Playoff contests. Taken No. 5 overall by the Leafs in the 2012 NHL Entry Draft, Rielly spent parts of three seasons in the Western Hockey League with the Moose Jaw Warriors. He finished with 21 goals and 79 assists for 100 points in 143 career regular-season games. He also had nine assists in 11 WHL playoff games. Internationally, Rielly represented Canada at the World Championships multiple times and helped them win a gold medal in 2016. He was also part of the 2013 World Junior Championship roster.

items.body: The Montreal Canadiens likely will get a big boost late in the 2025-26 season, even if they don't do anything huge at the trade deadline. Top prospect Michael Hage (Michigan, NCAA) and second-round pick Alexander Zharovsky (Salavat Yulaev Ufa, KHL) are expected to be available to play for the Canadiens late this season after their respective campaigns conclude, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported on Saturday Headlines . Nate Schmidt will be held out of the matchup due to a day-to-day, upper-body injury. Schmidt only played in four minutes of Utah’s Thursday loss to the Montreal Canadiens. He took a hard hit from Canadiens’ forward Nick Suzuki in one of his final shifts and was in noticeable pain in subsequent shifts. Utah recalled Gregor Biber on Friday. The 20 year old will sit out of Saturday’s matchup in favor of Artyom Duda, who has no points and a minus-three through the first two games of his NHL career. The Mammoth are already facing an injury to John Marino , who fell out of the lineup on October 17th with an upper-body injury. Nick DeSimone has filled in for Marino’s hole on the right-side – though Biber is on the cusp of his NHL debut should Utah want to replace either Duda or DeSimone. Like with Marino, the Mammoth will have no immediate replacement for Schmidt’s impact. The 35 year old continues to do it all – with four points, 14 shot blocks, and 20 hits through 17 games this season. Schmidt has averaged 19 minutes of ice time per game, continuing a trend that began with his first season in Utah last year. The Mammoth will lean on rookies – either Duda or Biber – to make up for that two-way presence until Schmidt is back to full health.

It has been a rocky season for the 22-year-old Salomonsson. Arniel has continued to lean on the young defender despite those struggles, deploying him for 18:20 a game on average. That’s an uptick from Salomonsson’s usage in his rookie season last year – which was marked by five points and 17:58 in average ice time through 32 games. items.title: Rangers, James Reimer Contract Termination Echoes Historically Harsh Reality For Multiple Longtime NHL Goaltenders
items.summary: The New York Rangers have mutually agreed to terminate the contract of goalie James Reimer on Saturday. But while this is likely the end of Reimer's NHL career, his longevity is to be admired. Even the best goalies end their NHL careers in a non-ideal manner.
items.body: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Rangers, James Reimer Contract Termination Echoes Historically Harsh Reality For Multiple Longtime NHL Goaltenders Adam Proteau Partner Nov 7, 2026 11:31 PM Published Nov 7, 2026 11:31 PM The New York Rangers have mutually agreed to terminate the contract of goalie James Reimer on Saturday. But while this is likely the end of Reimer's NHL career, his longevity is to be admired. Even the best goalies end their NHL careers in a non-ideal manner. Being an NHL-caliber goaltender is one of the toughest jobs in professional sports. If you’re one of the precious few who can consistently put in needle-moving efforts for your team, the world’s your oyster. But even then, at the tail end of your career, your power slips through your fingers and you find yourself exiting the game on terms you wouldn’t prefer. The latest example of that is journeyman netminder James Reimer. The veteran goalie was placed on waivers for the purpose of contract termination by the New York Rangers on Saturday, mutually agreeing to part ways off his one-year contract. items.body: Register Login Rangers’ Alberts Smits Out With Upper-Body Injury By Gabriel Foley | at November 7, 2026 5:09 pm The New York Rangers made a change to the lineup just before Saturday’s matchup against the Seattle Kraken. Rookie defenseman and reigning fifth-overall pick Alberts Smits was pulled out due to an upper-body injury per Vince Z. Mercogliano of The Athletic . Matthew Robertson made his season debut in Smits’ absence. Smits will record the first absence of his young NHL career with this news. The 18 year old has struggled through the onset of the season, with no scoring, 12 penalty minutes, and a minus-two in 17 games so far. He has generally stood as New York’s sixth defenseman, recording between 10 and 16 minutes of ice time each game. Smits was lauded for his productive pro appearances last season – marked by 13 points in 38 games in Finland’s Liiga and seven points in 16 games in Germany’ DEL. He also notched two points in four games at the 2026 Winter Olympics and four points in eight games at the World Championship. Despite a productive draft year that earned Smits the title of most NHL-ready from many draft pundits, the Latvian blue-liner has failed to find his spark in the Rangers lineup just yet. New York is clearly committed to keeping Smits in their rotation – but a brief absence could give the rookie a chance to find the jump that led him to strong scoring last year. He is a mobile, puck-moving defender at his best. A path to production in New York will come after Smits finds a way back into that role at the NHL level. In the meantime, Robertson will return to the NHL lineup after beginning the year in the minor-leagues. items.title: ‘Extremely grateful’: Price, Bergeron headline 2026 Hockey Hall of Fame class
items.body: TORONTO — Carey Price spent a lot of his youth on the road and in the air. Growing up in a remote part of British Columbia, that's what chasing his hockey dream required. When the phone rang in June to announce he would be joining the game's greats, Price was fittingly in a familiar situation — driving. "I was on my way to go visit my grandmother at the hospital," recalled the former Montreal Canadiens goaltender. "Hockey Hall of Fame came up with my caller ID in my truck, so pretty excited about that. Got to spend the rest of the day with my grandmother, who made a recovery. Price had plenty of those in the NHL and with Canada on the international stage. Now he will share another one Monday with the rest of the hall's 2026 class. The netminder headlines this year's inductees alongside Patrice Bergeron, Pekka Rinne, Keith Tkachuk and Cindy Curley in the player category set to be enshrined Monday. Brian Burke will go in as a builder. "A long road to get to this point," Price, who starred in Montreal for all 15 of his NHL seasons and will enter the hall in his second year of eligibility, said Saturday. "I'm just extremely thankful for that journey and everything that I learned along the way — not only in hockey but in life." The No. 5 pick at the 2005 draft, Price won the Hart Trophy as league MVP and the Vezina Trophy as its top goaltender in 2015. The 39-year-old from Anahim Lake, B.C., finished with a 361-261-79 record, .917 save percentage, 2.51 goals-against average and 49 shutouts across 712 regular-season games in a career that was, at times, hampered by injury. Price had even better big-moment numbers before a knee issue forced him to stop playing beyond the 2021-22 campaign.
